questions.prompt: A BJT with \(V_A = 60\ \mathrm{V}\) carries \(I_C = 1.00\ \mathrm{mA}\) at \(V_{CE} = 2\ \mathrm{V}\). Using \(I_C \propto (1 + V_{CE}/V_A)\), what is \(I_C\) at \(V_{CE} = 8\ \mathrm{V}\) (in mA)?
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: What is the output resistance \(r_o = V_A/I_C\) (in kΩ) for \(V_A = 60\ \mathrm{V}\), \(I_C = 0.5\ \mathrm{mA}\)?
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: What is the physical cause of the Early effect?
options: Base-width modulation: more \(V_{CB}\) widens the collector depletion region into the base
questions.explanation: A thinner neutral base gives a steeper electron gradient and more \(I_C\) (reader Sec. 11.6.3).
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: Extending the forward-active curves backward, where do they meet?
options: Near \(V_{CE} = -V_A\) on the voltage axis, for all bias currents
They are parallel and never meet
questions.explanation: Each curve is \(I_{C0}(1 + V_{CE}/V_A)\), which is zero at \(V_{CE} = -V_A\) whatever \(I_{C0}\) is.
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: Doubling \(I_C\) from 0.4 mA to 0.8 mA with \(V_A = 40\ \mathrm{V}\) changes \(r_o\) from 100 kΩ to what (in kΩ)?
questions.explanation: \(r_o = V_A/I_C = 40/0.8\ \mathrm{mA} = 50\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\): \(r_o\) is inversely proportional to bias current.
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: Measured: \(I_C = 2.00\ \mathrm{mA}\) at \(V_{CE} = 3\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(2.08\ \mathrm{mA}\) at \(V_{CE} = 7\ \mathrm{V}\). Extract \(V_A\) in V.
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: An ideal current source (infinite resistance) is approximated by a BJT with \(V_A = 80\ \mathrm{V}\) at \(I_C = 0.2\ \mathrm{mA}\). If \(V_{CE}\) swings by 2 V, by how many µA does \(I_C\) change?
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: Which BJT design choice gives a larger Early voltage?
options: A more heavily doped base (less depletion spreads into it)
questions.explanation: Base-width modulation is weaker when the depletion region extends mostly into the collector, i.e. \(N_B \gg N_C\). (It trades against \(\beta\).)
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: The Early voltage in BJTs plays the same role as which MOSFET parameter?
questions.explanation: Both describe how the output current rises with output voltage, and both give \(r_o = V_A/I\) (reader Eq. 8.40), so the same small-signal reasoning carries over between the two devices.
questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.figure_alt: Collector curves in forward-active sloping upward; extended backward to negative V_CE they all meet the axis near V_CE = -V_A, the Early voltage.

questions.prompt: Preview of the small-signal model: where does \(r_o\) appear in the BJT small-signal model?
options: Between collector and emitter, in parallel with the \(g_mv_{be}\) source
questions.explanation: It models the slope of the \(I_C\)-\(V_{CE}\) curve, just like the MOSFET's \(r_o\).

questions.prompt: Preview of the BJT small-signal model: the intrinsic gain \(g_mr_o\) of a BJT is typically much higher than a MOSFET's at similar current. Why?
options: BJT \(g_m = I_C/V_{th}\) is larger than MOSFET \(g_m = 2I_D/V_{ov}\) when \(V_{ov} > 2V_{th}\)
questions.explanation: Per unit current, the exponential is steeper than the square law at practical overdrives.
